page: UpCloud STARTER-1xCPU-1GB is a budget-focused virtual server built on the KVM hypervisor. It features a single shared vCPU from the AMD EPYC 9575F processor family, running at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz on the x86_64 architecture. This single-core, single-thread configuration is paired with 1.0 GB of system memory and a bundled 10 GB local SSD. The CPU includes advanced instruction sets such as AVX-512, AVX_VNNI, and hardware-accelerated cryptography via AES and SHA_NI.

In benchmark evaluations, the server demonstrates highly polarized performance characteristics. Due to its modern AMD EPYC architecture, single-core CPU performance in stress-ng is rated in the top tier. However, because of the single-vCPU limitation and shared resource allocation, multi-core CPU performance and PassMark CPU scores fall into the bottom 25%. Memory performance is similarly constrained, with read-only bandwidth benchmarks scoring in the bottom 25%, and PassMark memory and database operations registering at the bottom 10%. Large block memory write bandwidth remains average at 29.5 GB/sec.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, this server represents a low-cost entry point for lightweight workloads, offering modern CPU instructions at a minimal resource density. The primary tradeoff is the strict 1.0 GB memory limit and shared CPU allocation, which makes it unsuitable for memory-intensive applications or sustained multi-threaded processing. It is best suited for basic utility tasks, lightweight static web serving, simple cron jobs, or development and testing environments that do not require high memory or sustained multi-core throughput.
